subject: Reserved capacity playbook & discount escalation — Cobalt Labs
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-12-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Cobalt — sizing scenarios + delegated discount ask

Team,

Attaching the initial Cobalt proposal (cobalt_proposal_v1.pdf). They want to lock a reserved pool tied to their upcoming product launch. Quick summary:
- Request: 12 x A100-ish equivalent GPUs (24/7), baseline throughput target 6M tokens/day.
- Term requested: 12 months firm, then auto-renew unless notice.
- Cobalt asks for flexibility to scale + an 18-month option if they hit growth milestones.

Key asks for internal alignment:
1) Sizing scenarios — is 12 dedicated units defensible or do we recommend bucketed burst capacity + guaranteed baseline?
2) Discount approval — they expect 22–25% off list for a 12mo commit with co-marketing. What's our delegated approval threshold?
3) GPU price sensitivity — if market rates rise >15% vs our forecast, they want an indexation conversation. Should we offer a pass-through floor or a cap?

Laura, can you run quick cost scenarios (base/upsell/growth) and call out where discounts push margin below our threshold? Marissa, want you in the loop for negotiation cadence and whether we can offer a one-time onboarding credit. Grace, can you flag any product-side constraints on burst sizing or KV-cache warmup that would affect perf?

Desired next step: have an agreed playbook by EOD so I can share a revised proposal with Cobalt.

Attachments: cobalt_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal summary, SOW stub)

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-12-07T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cobalt — sizing scenarios + delegated discount ask

Jonas —

Rapid cost scenarios attached (cost-scenarios.xlsx). High level:
- Base (12 A100 equiv, 12mo): expected gross margin ~39% at list price.
- With 22% discount: margin drops to ~26%.
- At 25% discount: margin ~23% — below our preferred floor for reserved deals unless covered by a risk escrow or guaranteed upsell.

GPU price sensitivity: if we index to market and prices rise >15%, we should include a trigger that allows us to either: 1) pass-through incremental costs above threshold, or 2) reduce reserved-hours commitment prorata. Finance prefers option 1 with a capped annual adjustment (e.g., max +10% in year).

Delegated approvals: my note — sales can approve up to 20% discount for deals <= $1.2M ARR. Anything above that needs manager/finance sign-off. If Marissa can get co-marketing commitment or guaranteed ramp milestones that release a $200k onboarding credit, we can tolerate 22% for the first 6 months.

I've flagged the cells where unit economics slip and included a simple sensitivity table.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference
From: Natalie Reed <natalie@cobaltlabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@cobaltlabs.com
Date: 2026-12-07T13:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cobalt — sizing scenarios + delegated discount ask

Thanks Jonas — and thanks Laura for the transparency. A few clarifications from our side:

- We are prepared to commit to 12 GPUs for 12 months if we can secure a 22% discount and an option to extend to 18 months at a pre-agreed step-down price.
- We need a safety buffer (we're a user-facing product) — can Redwood offer a 20% burst pool above baseline for peak events at a higher metered rate?
- About indexation: we appreciate a capped adjustment. If we agree to +10% cap in year, we would also like a right to pause new workloads for 60 days if there is a >20% upstream market shock.

We can move quickly if legal can work the SOW and we get a term sheet that includes the above.

Natalie Reed
Head of Infrastructure — Cobalt Labs
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Reed <natalie@cobaltlabs.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T16:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cobalt — sizing scenarios + delegated discount ask

Natalie — appreciate the clarity and speed. Proposal from our side to get this over the line: 

1) Commercial: 12 GPU reserved baseline for 12 months at 22% discount, with a predefined extension option to 18 months (price step-down applies on extension).
2) Burst: we provide a 15% shared burst pool for the first 90 days; additional burst capacity available at metered rates (we will outline the uplift).
3) Indexation / shocks: agree to an annual indexation with an upper cap of +10% on unit price. For systemic market shocks >20%, Redwood can trigger a 60-day operational review with temporary limitations on new workload onboarding (not retroactive on in-flight requests).
4) Conditions: Discount is contingent on a $150k onboarding credit and a case study commitment at launch.

Next steps: Laura/Finance — confirm margin runway on the revised structure (22% + $150k credit + burst uplift). Markus — can you confirm delegated approval path? If we have signoff, legal to draft SOW and we send a term sheet by Friday.

Thanks — I'll hold a slot for an accelerated signature once we have finance + markus greenlight.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-12-08T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cobalt — sizing scenarios + delegated discount ask

Marissa / team —

Reviewed Laura's scenarios and Marissa's updated commercial compromise. I approve up to a 23% discount for this deal provided we implement the following controls before signature:
- A $150k onboarding credit sits in a short-term escrow and is refundable against missed ramp milestones (define milestones in SOW).
- Legal to include the annual indexation language capped at +10% and explicit language around a 60-day operational pause for systemic market shocks >20%.
- Finance to provide a contingency line showing margin at 23% discount and expected NPV.

Once those three controls are documented, proceed to final term sheet and SOW. If anything deviates materially, loop me back.

Markus Klein
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
